entry.title: Strongly Adaptive Asynchronous Byzantine Agreement with Linear Communication and Almost-Everywhere Termination
entry.summary:
It is well known that Byzantine agreement requires $\Omega(t^2)$ messages against a strongly adaptive adversary that may corrupt $t=\Theta(n)$ parties and suppress a party's undelivered messages upon corruption. We circumvent this lower bound by relaxing termination: for any constant $0<\nu<1$, at least a $(1-\nu)$ fraction of the honest parties terminate, while agreement and validity hold for every honest decision. For every constant corruption gap $\delta>0$ and every $t\leq(1-\delta)n/3$, we construct binary agreement with this guarantee in authenticated asynchronous networks against strongly adaptive corruptions with message takebacks.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: When Elliptic-Curve Semiprimality Certificates Reveal Factors
entry.summary:
Public certificates of semiprimality could support cryptographic modulus generation by proving that an integer has exactly two prime factors without revealing them. Their usefulness in this setting depends on whether the certificate preserves the difficulty of factoring. Motivated by the examples of Reble and Broadhurst, we formalize semiprimality certificates by adapting the Goldwasser-Kilian primality criterion.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #logic

entry.title: Amortized Multi-Verifier Proofs from Reductions of Knowledge
entry.summary:
We study amortization of prover work in the multi-verifier setting, motivated by proof-as-a-service deployments in which a shared prover serves $K$ independent clients holding distinct statements. Each verifier checks only its own statement and proof, with no inter-verifier communication. The challenge is therefore to amortize prover work across many proofs while preserving local verification.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: Smaller Share Size for Evolving Secret Sharing: General Thresholds and Threshold Three
entry.summary:
Evolving secret sharing allows participants to join indefinitely without modifying previously distributed shares. We study the share size of perfectly secure evolving threshold secret sharing schemes and obtain two improvements. For general thresholds, we introduce a polynomial sharing method that shares two secrets with adjacent reconstruction thresholds using one polynomial.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems

entry.title: Proofs of Quantum Memory
entry.summary:
With the rapid advances in quantum computer architectures and the emerging prospect of large-scale quantum memory, it is becoming essential to classically verify that remote devices genuinely allocate the promised quantum memory with a specified number of qubits. In this paper, we introduce a new concept, proofs of quantum memory (PoQM). A PoQM is an interactive protocol between a classical probabilistic polynomial-time (PPT) verifier and a quantum polynomial-time (QPT) prover over a classical channel where the verifier can verify that the prover has possessed a quantum memory with a specified number of qubits for a specified period of time.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #quantum-computing
